thesis: Micron's stock continues an AI-memory supercycle move (+12.95% over 60 days) built on already-disclosed HBM4 sold-out, take-or-pay contracts (~$100B) and a Q3 beat/raise, though much of the current strength reflects positioning ahead of the 9/30 earnings print rather than a single new confirmed catalyst this window. Two unresolved pullbacks occurred inside the window (on CXMT's public debut and AI-capex-slowdown commentary), so the bar this rally sets hasn't been tested by an actual print yet.
invalidation: A weak Q4 FY2026 print (reported 9/30), a guidance cut, or confirmation that CXMT or other Chinese memory suppliers are meaningfully undercutting Micron's contracted HBM pricing would undermine the thesis.
sources: Micron Investor Relations Q3 FY2026 results: https://investors.micron.com
Tom's Hardware (DRAM price-fixing class action, 6/29-30/26): tomshardware.com

thesis: AAPL's volume spike coincides with today's iPhone 18 Pro launch/in-store availability, a confirmed company event, but a same-day UBS note flagged shorter-than-expected pre-order wait times as a muted early-demand signal that hasn't been resolved by actual sell-through data yet.
invalidation: Confirmed weak iPhone 18 sell-through in coming weeks, or an adverse outcome on Apple's EU DMA compliance deadline (Oct 2026), would undermine the thesis.
sources: MT Newswires via ad-hoc-news.de (UBS muted demand note, 9/18/26): ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/corporate-news/apple-stock-gains-as-bank-of-america-keeps-a-370-target/70124181
newsbytesapp.com (EU DMA October 2026 compliance deadline): newsbytesapp.com

thesis: SPCX's sharp 60-day move and volume spike reflect a string of confirmed catalysts (the xAI and Cursor acquisitions, Nasdaq-100 inclusion, a Q2 beat) layered with speculative Musk merger-hint commentary that has not produced any confirmed deal. The FAA's mishap investigation from the May Starship failure remains an open compliance gate, with the next Starship flight (slipped from 9/22 to 9/28) serving as the return-to-flight test.
invalidation: A failed or further-delayed Starship return-to-flight, or any sign the FAA compliance process is not resolving favorably, would undermine the thesis.

thesis: BorgWarner's volume spike follows JPMorgan naming it a top U.S. auto-supplier pick (citing hybrid/ICE resilience and early data-center turbine-generator revenue) layered on a real Q2 beat and raised guidance -- but this is analyst-opinion-driven rather than a fresh company disclosure. A subsequent UBS downgrade on valuation concerns remains unaddressed.
invalidation: A reversal of the JPMorgan thesis, weak turbine-generator order flow, or confirmation the UBS valuation concern is warranted would undermine the case.
sources: BorgWarner IR press release (Q2 2026 results/buyback increase, 8/5/26): borgwarner.com/newsroom/press-releases/2026/08/05

thesis: Intel's 60-day gain reflects a real Q2 beat and Fortinet's confirmed 18A foundry win, alongside speculative reports of an SK hynix Ohio-fab arrangement that Intel itself says isn't finalized. The company also completed a $20B common stock offering in early August 2026 -- a real, disclosed dilution event inside the lookback window.
invalidation: If the SK hynix talks fall through or foundry customer momentum stalls, the bull case weakens; the dilution from the August raise is already a known drag on per-share metrics regardless.

thesis: Dell's very large 60-day move is grounded in a confirmed, record Q2 FY2027 beat (record AI-server orders and $95B backlog) and a meaningful FY guidance raise -- a genuine, already-disclosed catalyst. Separately, Dell's FY2025 10-K disclosed a correction of understated COGS tied to 'actions of certain employees' in one segment, with internal controls deemed ineffective at the time -- a disclosed governance event inside the 3-year lookback, even though the company characterized it as a revision rather than a formal Item 4.02 restatement.
invalidation: Margin compression from the AI-server mix shift, a slowdown in hyperscaler AI capex, or a repeat internal-controls finding would undermine the thesis.

thesis: Pure Storage/Everpure's move combines confirmed fundamentals (a hyperscaler design win, a Q2 beat-and-raise, an activist stake from Jana Partners) with today's extreme volume spike being largely a mechanical S&P 500 index-inclusion effect (effective 9/21) rather than new fundamental news. UBS held a Sell rating through the rally on valuation, a concern the company hasn't directly addressed.
invalidation: A post-inclusion fade in the index-flow-driven volume without follow-through fundamental strength, or confirmation the UBS valuation concern is warranted, would undermine the thesis.

thesis: Illumina's volume spike is explicitly attributed by analysts to mechanical S&P 500 index-inclusion buying (effective 9/21) layered on a real FY guidance raise, with some flagging 'sharp downside risk once forced buying subsides.' A Delaware Chancery hearing to approve dismissal of derivative litigation tied to the GRAIL reacquisition is scheduled for 11/2/26, inside the near-term window.
invalidation: A post-inclusion fade once passive index flows subside, or an unfavorable turn in the Delaware court proceeding, would undermine the thesis.

thesis: Csquare's decline and volume spike mix a real, sector-wide AI/data-center selloff (macro, not company-specific) with company-specific leverage concerns (~$5.76B debt against ~$120M cash) flagged by Morgan Stanley, against a backdrop of genuinely strong Q2 results and 9 of 10 covering analysts rating it Buy. The evidence here is mixed and offsetting rather than pointing to a clear net read.
invalidation: A resolution of the leverage overhang, or confirmation the AI/data-center selloff is purely macro/sector-wide rather than also company-specific, would reopen the case for entry; for now the thesis is inconclusive.

thesis: AXTI's continued strength rests on a real Q2 beat-and-raise (record indium phosphide substrate demand for AI/optical networking, backlog >$100M) plus S&P SmallCap 600 inclusion effective 9/21, though the most recent leg of the rally is amplified by index flows and newly launched leveraged ETFs on the name. Roughly $43M in trailing-90-day insider selling and continued dependence on Chinese export-license approvals (light as recently as Q1 2026) are real, unresolved counterweights.
invalidation: A renewed export-license delay from Chinese authorities, a guidance miss, or continued heavy insider selling without offsetting fundamental news would argue for exiting rather than holding.
sources: MT Newswires (Q2 2026 beat, 7/30-31/26): via Robinhood news feed

thesis: SK hynix's strength is grounded in a real, ongoing DRAM/HBM shortage (CEO says it could last through 2030) and confirmed HBM4 lead-supplier status for Nvidia's Rubin platform, but the company completed a $29.65B Nasdaq ADR offering in July 2026 -- a real dilution event inside the 90-day window. Analysts themselves flag sentiment as stretched and vulnerable to a 'sell the peak' reversal.
invalidation: Confirmation of memory-price weakness or oversupply, or a sharp 'sell the peak' reversal once shortage optimism cools, would argue for exiting rather than holding.

thesis: Marvell's recent strength is grounded in a real, confirmed Q2 FY2027 record beat with raised FY27/FY28 guidance on custom AI-silicon demand, though the stock remains ~26% below its 52-week high after a sector-wide AI-capex-sentiment selloff (a September 14 single-day drop tied to Anthropic-essay-driven AI-slowdown fears, not company-specific news). Valuation remains stretched (>70x trailing P/E), a concern the quarter's results don't fully resolve.
invalidation: Evidence that AWS or another hyperscaler customer is meaningfully diversifying away from Marvell's custom silicon, or a guidance cut, would argue for exiting rather than holding.
sources: Marvell Investor Relations (Q2 FY2027 results, 8/27/26): investor.marvell.com
Yahoo Finance / Motley Fool (Sept 14 AI-slowdown-fear selloff): finance.yahoo.com
Marvell IR (CFO transition press release, 6/11/26): investor.marvell.com

thesis: Nvidia's Q2 FY2027 print showed continued strong ex-China growth (~106% YoY) even as management guided China data-center compute revenue to zero going forward -- a real, disclosed demand loss offsetting real, disclosed strength elsewhere. Custom AI ASICs from Broadcom/Marvell-designed chips continue gaining inference-workload share, though Nvidia's training/CUDA moat appears intact for now.
invalidation: Evidence that ex-China hyperscaler demand is also softening, or that custom ASICs are displacing Nvidia in training workloads (not just inference), would argue for exiting rather than holding.
sources: CNBC (Q2 FY2027 earnings, China guided to zero, 8/26/26): cnbc.com/2026/08/26/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q2-2027-live-updates.html
